lookups.evidenceParaphrase: The Japanese dictionary explicitly distinguishes native うじ as a respectful surname suffix, with an attested 1825 example, and explains that this suffix receded as on-reading し took the same role in modern times. The encyclopedia explicitly illustrates 山田氏 with suffix reading うじ.
lookups.teachingDisposition: Use 山田氏 やまだうじ solely as a qualified older suffix example for metadata -うじ; contrast modern reporting やまだし. Do not infer this reading from the ordinary clan-name 源氏 げんじ or invent a new surname's pronunciation.
